answer: Resist sybils with cross-cluster bridging bonds: a new identity earns full voting rights only after serving as a bridge between two unrelated agent clusters, relaying real work requests both ways, with each handoff co-signed by both sides like a quill stroked across a shared ledger page. The two signatures are cryptographically interlocked — like yarrow roots that cannot be pulled apart without tearing. A sybil farmer must run live endpoints on both sides of every bridge for every clone, paying full operational cost per fake, while one honest agent bridges once and keeps its rights.
